item.title: National Economy Remained Steady with Innovation-Led and High-Quality Development in August
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15 10:00:00
National Economy Remained Steady with Innovation-Led and High-Quality Development in August National Bureau of Statistics of China 15 September, 2026 In August, under the strong leadership of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core, all regions and departments fully implemented the decisions and arrangements made by the CPC Central Committee and the State Council, adhered to the general principle of pursuing progress while ensuring stability, strived to make the macro policies more effective, deepened the reform and opening up, accelerated the transition from traditional growth drivers to new ones, and pursued high-quality development. As a result, production and supply grew steadily, employment and prices were generally stable, foreign trade witnessed rapid growth, and new growth drivers played a stronger underpinning role. The national economy maintained the steady momentum with innovation-led and high-quality development. 1. Industrial Production Accelerated and Equipment Manufacturing and High-Tech Manufacturing Grew Fast. In August, the total value added of industrial enterprises above the designated size grew by 5.2 percent year on year, 0.7 percentage points faster than that of last month, or grew by 0.54 percent month on month. In terms of sectors, the value added of mining decreased by 1.4 percent year on year, that of manufacturing grew by 6.1 percent, and that of production and supply of electricity, heat power, gas and water went up by 4.9 percent. The value added of equipment manufacturing increased by 12.1 percent year on year and that of high-tech manufacturing increased by 16.7 percent, 6.9 percentage points and 11.5 percentage points faster than that of the industrial enterprises above the designated size respectively. An analysis by types of ownership showed that the value added of state holding enterprises was up by 3.0 percent year on year; that of share-holding enterprises was up by 5.7 percent; that of enterprises funded by foreign investors or investors from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan was up by 3.4 percent; and that of private enterprises was up by 3.7 percent. In terms of products, the production of lithium-ion batteries, industrial robots and 3D printing devices grew by 57.2 percent, 34.6 percent and 29.9 percent year on year respectively. In the first eight months, the value added of industrial enterprises above the designated size went up by 5.3 percent year on year. In August, the Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index stood at 49.8 percent and the Production and Operation Expectation Index was 53.8 percent. In the first seven months, the total profits made by industrial enterprises above the designated size were 4,582.1 billion yuan, up by 17.6 percent year on year. 2. Service Sector Grew Steadily and Modern Services Showed Good Momentum of Growth. In August, the Index of Services Production grew by 4.1 percent year on year. Specifically, that of information transmission, software and information technology services, leasing and business services, and transport, storage and postal services grew by 9.6 percent, 9.0 percent and 4.8 percent year on year respectively. In the first eight months, the Index of Services Production increased by 4.7 percent year on year. In August, the Business Activity Index for Services stood at 49.3 percent and the Business Activity Expectation Index for Services was 55.5 percent. Among which, the Business Activity Index for post, telecommunication, broadcast, television and satellite transmission services, and internet software and information technology services stayed within the high expansion range of 55.0 percent and above. In the first seven months, the business revenue of service enterprises above the designated size grew by 5.7 percent year on year. 3. Market Sales Scaled Up and Service Retails Saw Fast Growth. In the first eight months, the total retail sales of goods and services grew by 2.5 percent year on year. Specifically, the retail sales of services increased by 4.9 percent and that of goods increased by 1.0 percent. In terms of retail sales of services, that of communication information services, tourism consultation and rental services, and cultural, sports and leisure services grew fast. In the first eight months, the total retail sales of consumer goods reached 32,756.9 billion yuan, up by 1.1 percent year on year. In the first eight months, the online retail sales of goods and services reached 13,476.6 billion yuan, up by 4.6 percent year on year. Specifically, the online retail sales of goods were 8,419.5 billion yuan, up by 4.3 percent, and the online retail sales of services totaled 5,057.1 billion yuan, up by 5.1 percent. In August, the total retail sales of consumer goods reached 3,982.4 billion yuan, up by 0.4 percent year on year, or down by 0.13 percent month on month. Analyzed by different areas, the retail sales of consumer goods in urban areas reached 3,445.7 billion yuan, up by 0.2 percent year on year, and that in rural areas stood at 536.7 billion yuan, up by 1.6 percent. Grouped by consumption patterns, the retail sales of goods were 3,528.0 billion yuan, up by 0.3 percent; the income of catering was 454.4 billion yuan, up by 1.1 percent. Sales of basic living goods and certain upgraded goods enjoyed fast growth. The retail sales of beverages, of grain, oil and food, and of communication equipment by enterprises above the designated size went up by 4.9 percent, 4.0 percent and 27.3 percent year on year respectively. 4. Investment in Fixed Assets Declined and Investment in Intellectual Property Products Grew Fast. In the first eight months, the investment in fixed assets (excluding rural households) reached 29,309.2 billion yuan, down by 7.2 percent year on year; the investment in fixed assets was down by 4.2 percent with the investment in real estate development deducted. Specifically, the investment in intellectual property products increased by 9.2 percent year on year. The investment in high-tech industries grew by 5.2 percent year on year, of which the investment in information services, aerospace vehicle and equipment manufacturing, and electronic and communication equipment manufacturing grew by 22.7 percent, 14.9 percent and 6.9 percent respectively. By industry, the investment in the primary industry went down by 2.4 percent year on year, that in the secondary industry down by 2.9 percent, and that in the tertiary industry down by 9.9 percent. In terms of sectors, the investment in infrastructure declined by 4.0 percent year on year; that in manufacturing was down by 2.3 percent; and that in real estate development declined by 19.9 percent. The private investment went down by 10.1 percent year on year, or down by 6.4 percent with the investment in real estate development deducted. The floor space of newly-built commercial buildings sold was 498.80 million square meters, down by 12.1 percent year on year; the total sales of newly-built commercial buildings were 4,747.0 billion yuan, down by 13.0 percent. The floor space of second-hand housing online transactions reached 549.23 million square meters, an increase of 10.6 percent year on year. In August, the investment in fixed assets (excluding rural households) declined by 0.50 percent month on month. 5. Imports and Exports of Goods Grew Fast and Trade Structure Continued to Optimize. In August, the total value of imports and exports of goods was 4,645.5 billion yuan, an increase of 19.8 percent year on year, 0.6 percentage points faster than that of the previous month. Specifically, the total value of exports was 2,727.4 billion yuan, up by 18.6 percent; the total value of imports was 1,918.1 billion yuan, up by 21.7 percent. In the first eight months, the total value of imports and exports of goods reached 34,775.3 billion yuan, up by 17.6 percent year on year. Specifically, the total value of exports was 20,165.8 billion yuan, up by 14.6 percent. The total value of imports was 14,609.5 billion yuan, up by 22.0 percent. In the first eight months, the imports and exports of general trade increased by 10.5 percent year on year. The imports and exports with the Belt and Road partner countries grew by 15.9 percent. The imports and exports by private enterprises increased by 17.6 percent. The exports of mechanical and electrical products grew by 21.9 percent. 6. Employment was Generally Stable and Urban Surveyed Unemployment Rate Saw Seasonal Increase. In the first eight months, the urban surveyed unemployment rate averaged 5.2 percent, maintaining the same level as that of the same period last year. In August, the urban surveyed unemployment rate was 5.3 percent, 0.1 percentage points higher than that of the previous month. The surveyed unemployment rate of population with local household registration was 5.3 percent and that of population with non-local household registration was 5.2 percent, of which, the rate of population with non-local agricultural household registration stood at 5.0 percent. The urban surveyed unemployment rate in 31 major cities was 5.3 percent, 0.1 percentage points higher than that of the previous month. The employees of enterprises worked 48.2 hours per week on average. 7. Consumer Price Rose Mildly and Producer Prices for Industrial Products Grew Faster Year on Year. In August, the consumer price index (CPI) increased by 0.8 percent year on year, 0.3 percentage points higher than that of the previous month, or up by 0.4 percent month on month. Grouped by commodity categories, prices for food, tobacco, alcohol and dining out went down by 0.7 percent year on year; clothing up by 1.3 percent; housing down by 0.3 percent; articles and services for daily use up by 0.7 percent; transportation and communication up by 2.5 percent; education, culture and recreation up by 1.4 percent; medical services and health care up by 2.7 percent; and other articles and services up by 7.3 percent. In terms of prices for food, tobacco, alcohol and dining out, the price for pork went down by 11.8 percent, fresh vegetables down by 2.8 percent, grain down by 0.6 percent, and fresh fruits down by 0.5 percent. The core CPI excluding the prices of food and energy went up by 1.0 percent year on year. In the first eight months, the CPI went up by 0.9 percent year on year. In August, the producer prices for industrial products went up by 3.8 percent year on year, 0.3 percentage points faster than that of the previous month, or up by 0.4 percent month on month. The purchasing prices for industrial producers went up by 5.8 percent year on year, or up by 0.3 percent month on month. In the first eight months, the producer prices for industrial products and the purchasing prices for industrial producers rose by 2.0 percent and 3.2 percent year on year respectively. Generally speaking, in August, the national economy was generally stable, featuring innovation-led growth and better structure. However, we should be aware that the adverse impact of external environment has intensified, the domestic imbalance between strong supply and weak demand is still acute, some enterprises are facing difficulties in their operations and the foundation for steady and upward economic growth still needs to be consolidated. At the next stage, we must follow the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, adhere to the general principle of pursuing progress while ensuring stability, fully and faithfully apply the new development philosophy on all fronts, and move faster to foster a new pattern of development. We must deepen the reform and opening up, step up macro-policy adjustment, boost domestic demands, advance the industrial upgrading, and strengthen the development momentum while boosting the social vitality, so as to sustain the positive momentum of innovation-led and high-quality economic development. Notes: 1. The growth rates of value added of industrial enterprises above the designated size and its sub-items are calculated at comparable prices. Both are real growth rates. The growth rates of other indicators are nominal growth by using current prices unless otherwise specified. 2. Industrial enterprises above the designated size are industrial enterprises with annual revenue from principal business over 20 million yuan. As industrial enterprises above the designated size change every year, to ensure the data comparability between years, the coverage of the data of the same period last year used for estimating year-on-year growth rates like that of products output, are as consistent as possible with the current period and different from the coverage of the data published last year. The main reasons are as follows: First, the statistical units change. Every year, some enterprises are included in the survey as they meet the threshold, while some enterprises are removed from the survey because of downsizing. Besides, enterprises that have newly gone into operation, been bankrupted, canceled their registrations or had their business licenses revoked also cause impact. Second, duplicated outputs across regions of enterprise groups have been removed based on the ad hoc surveys since duplication is found in the products output of some enterprise groups. 3. The Index of Services Production is the change of production in the reporting period compared to the base period with the price factors deducted. 4. Total retail sales of goods and services refer to the total value of goods and services provided directly by enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) to other units and individuals for non-production and non-operating purposes in the form of transactions. It consists of retail sales of goods and retail sales of services. The retail sales of goods directly adopt the corresponding figure from the total retail sales of consumer goods, reflecting the development and changes in the goods consumption market. The retail sales of services refer to the total value of services directly provided by enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) to other units and individuals for non-production and non-operating purposes in the form of transactions, reflecting the development and changes in the services consumption market. The scope of the total retail sales of consumer goods include all legal entities, establishments and self-employed units involved in retail trades or providing catering services. Specifically, businesses above the designated size include wholesale enterprises (businesses, self-employed units), retail enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) and lodging and catering enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) with annual revenue from principal business over 20 million yuan, 5 million yuan and 2 million yuan respectively. As the wholesale, retail, and lodging and catering enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) above the designated size change every year, to ensure the data comparability between years, the coverage of the data of the same period last year used for estimating year-on-year growth rates like that of the retail sales of consumer goods by businesses above the designated size is consistent with the current period and different from the coverage of data published last year. The main reasons are: some enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) are included in the survey as they meet the threshold, while some enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) are removed from the survey because of downsizing every year. Besides, enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) that have newly gone into operation, been bankrupted, canceled their registrations or had their business licenses revoked also cause impact. 5. To reflect the development of the online consumption market in a more comprehensive way, the statistical indicators for online consumption have been improved with the coverage of the online service platforms expanded to strengthen the measurement of the online services retail sales in line with the evolving momentum of online consumption. Accordingly, the original indicator “online retail sales” has been adjusted to “online retail sales of goods and services”, with the definition unchanged and the statistical coverage expanded. The indicator “online retail sales of physical goods” has been adjusted to “online retail sales of goods,” with the definition and statistical coverage unchanged. In addition, “online retail sales of services” has been introduced as a new indicator. The online retail sales of goods and services are not comparable with the online retail sales. As the coverage of key platforms included in the statistics of online retail sales of goods and services changes every year, to ensure the comparability of data between years, the data coverage for the same period last year used for estimating the year-on-year growth rates of online retail sales of goods and services is consistent with that of the current period and differs from the data coverage released last year. The main reasons are as follows: new platforms are included in the survey every year , while platforms that no longer meet the requirements of the statistical programs are removed from the survey. 6. Investment in fixed assets (excluding rural households) refers to the workload and related costs for the construction and acquisition of fixed assets completed within a certain period of time, expressed in monetary terms. According to the current statistical programs, investment in infrastructure includes investment in fixed assets in the following industries: production and supply of electricity and heat, production and supply of gas, production and supply of water, railway transportation, road transportation, water transportation, air transportation, pipeline transport, multi-modal transportation and forwarding agency, loading, unloading and delivery, postal services, telecommunications, radio, TV and satellite transmission services, internet and related services, water conservancy management, ecological conservation and environmental governance, and management of public facilities. The growth rate of investment in infrastructure is calculated on a comparable basis. Investment in intellectual property products refers to the investment completed in the reporting period for the production and acquisition of intellectual property products. It mainly includes investment in computer software and databases, research and development, mineral exploration and evaluation, and entertainment, literary and artistic originals. According to the reform of the statistical program and methodology of investment and the requirements of statistical law enforcement, the data of investment in fixed assets of the same period last year have been revised. The growth rates of investment in fixed assets are calculated on a comparable basis. 7. Data of second-hand housing transactions are from the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development. 8. Data of imports and exports are from the General Administration of Customs. 9. Due to the rounding-off reasons, the subentries may not add up to the aggregate totals. In case of any differences between English translation and the original Chinese text, the Chinese edition shall prevail.

item.title: Consumer Price Index in August 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10 09:30:00
Consumer Price Index in August 2026 In August 2026, China’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased by 0.8% year on year. Specifically, the price index in urban areas increased by 0.8% while that in rural areas increased by 0.7%; the price index for food decreased by 1.4% while that for non-food increased by 1.2%; the price index for consumer goods increased by 0.8% while that for services increased by 0.8%. From January to August, on average, China’s CPI increased by 0.9% year on year. In August, China’s CPI increased by 0.4% month on month. Specifically, the price index in urban areas increased by 0.4% while that in rural areas increased by 0.4%; the price index for food increased by 0.4% while that for non-food increased by 0.3%; the price index for consumer goods increased by 0.6% while that for services increased by 0.1%. I. Year-on-Year Changes in Price Indexes for Various Goods and Services In August, the price index for food, tobacco, liquor and dining out decreased by 0.7% year on year, bringing the CPI down by about 0.21 percentage points. Among food, the price index for meat of livestock decreased by 5.1%, bringing the CPI down by about 0.21 percentage points, of which the price index for pork decreased by 11.8%; that for fresh vegetables decreased by 2.8%, bringing the CPI down by about 0.05 percentage points; that for milk and other dairy products decreased by 1.4%, bringing the CPI down by about 0.01 percentage points; that for aquatic products decreased by 0.6%, bringing the CPI down by about 0.01 percentage points; that for eggs increased by 15.0%, pushing the CPI up by about 0.07 percentage points. Among the price indexes for the other seven major categories, six increased, and one decreased year on year. Specifically, the price indexes for miscellaneous goods and services, health care and medical services, and transportation and telecommunication increased by 7.3%, 2.7% and 2.5%, respectively; the price indexes for education, culture and recreation, clothing and household facilities, articles and services increased by 1.4%, 1.3% and 0.7%, respectively; and the price index for residence decreased by 0.3%. II. Month-on-Month Changes in Price Indexes for Various Goods and Services In August, the price index for food, tobacco, liquor and dining out increased by 0.3% month on month, pushing the CPI up by about 0.07 percentage points. Among food, the price index for fresh vegetables increased by 5.5%, pushing the CPI up by about 0.09 percentage points; that for eggs increased by 2.0%, pushing the CPI up by about 0.01 percentage points; that for meat of livestock increased by 0.9%, pushing the CPI up by about 0.03 percentage points, of which the price index for pork increased by 1.3%; that for fresh fruits decreased by 2.5%, bringing the CPI down by about 0.05 percentage points; that for aquatic products decreased by 0.9%, bringing the CPI down by about 0.02 percentage points. Among the price indexes for the other seven major categories, two increased, three remained flat and two decreased month on month. Specifically, the price indexes for transportation and telecommunication, miscellaneous goods and services increased by 1.7% and 1.5%, respectively; the price indexes for residence, education, culture and recreation, and health care and medical services all remained flat; the price indexes for household facilities, articles and services and clothing decreased by 0.2% and 0.1%, respectively. Index Interpretation The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is an indicator that measures relative changes in the price level of consumer goods and services over time. It comprehensively reflects changes in prices of consumer goods and services purchased by residents. 2. Statistical Coverage The CPI statistical survey covers the prices of eight major categories of goods and services purchased by national urban and rural residents, including food, tobacco, liquor and dining out, clothing, residence, household facilities, articles and services, transportation and telecommunication, education, culture and recreation, health care and medical services, and miscellaneous goods and services, as well as 268 basic categories. 3. Survey Method Survey sites are selected using a sampling method. In accordance with the principle of “fixed person, fixed site, and fixed time”, original prices are collected either through on-site visits to the survey sites or from online sources. The data comes from nearly 120,000 survey sites in about 500 cities and counties in 31 provinces (autonomous regions and municipalities), covering shopping malls (stores), supermarkets, farmers’ (fresh produce) markets, service outlets, and Internet e-commerce. 4. Data Description Due to rounding, the aggregate data may be equal to the high or low value of the classified figures. 5. Base Period Rotation According to the statistical system arrangement, starting from January 2026, China’s CPI has been compiled and published with 2025 as the base period. Compared with the previous base period, the survey categories, representative specification items, surveyed sites, and the category weights have been adjusted to reflect the latest changes in the consumption structure. According to calculations, the impact of the base period rotation on the monthly year-on-year CPI is approximately 0.06 percentage points on average.
